source_standards: NBC 2016 Part 3 (General Building Requirements) — habitable rooms, kitchen, bathroom
NBC 2016 Part 4 (Fire and Life Safety) — staircase
IS 3861-2002 (Method of Measurement) — circulation factor derivation

_changelog.changes: S54 B-150 partial verification: fixed citations for POOJA / DINING / UTILITY / STORE / BALCONY / circulation_factor — these were incorrectly attributed to NBC clauses that don't exist. Values themselves unchanged in v2; full NBC PDF verification of STAIRCASE width + BALCONY area still pending under B-150 full.

notes: Values are NBC minimums where cited; ancillary rooms (pooja/dining/utility/store/balcony) use industry-typical values, NOT NBC mandates.
These are LOWER BOUNDS; if user's preferred_size is below, we reject.
Parity test verifies the two sources match exactly.

BATHROOM_ATTACHED.source_clause: NBC 2016 Part 3 cl. 6.2 (WC minimum 1.1 sqm; attached bath with basin = 1.8 sqm)

DINING.source_clause: Industry typical (no specific NBC mandate; dining typically subsumed under habitable-room area in NBC 2016 Part 3)

POOJA.source_clause: Industry typical (no NBC mandate; pooja rooms are cultural/optional, not regulated)

BALCONY.source_clause: Industry typical (NBC 2016 Part 3 cl. 6.3 covers balcony as habitable extension; specific area minimum varies by state/city DCR). Verify against PDF — possible 1.62 sqm if 0.9m × 1.8m is the canonical NBC reference.

UTILITY.source_clause: Industry typical (no NBC mandate; utility/washing areas not separately regulated in NBC 2016 Part 3)

STORE.source_clause: Industry typical (no NBC mandate; storage rooms not separately regulated in NBC 2016 Part 3)

STAIRCASE.source_clause: NBC 2016 Part 4 cl. 4.3.3 (staircase incl. landing). PDF VERIFICATION PENDING (B-150): width minimum is canonically 1.0m for residential, not 0.9m. The 5.5 sqm area derivation may need recalculation if 1.0m is correct.

circulation_factor.description: Multiplier on sum(room areas) to estimate total floor area. Wall thickness + horizontal corridors + vertical circulation typically add 30-35% overhead for residential. Small homes have proportionally more circulation; large homes are more efficient.
circulation_factor.source: Derived from IS 3861-2002 (Method of Measurement of Plinth, Carpet and Rentable Area) definitions; multiplier values themselves are engineer's-rule-of-thumb from industry surveys, NOT directly stipulated by IS 3861-2002. Survey: small homes 1.35-1.40, large homes 1.25-1.30, typical 1.30-1.35.
